user.title: Create Limit Helper
user.description: Categorize any numeric sensor into qualitative limit zones, evaluate single or double bounds (inside/outside range), with dynamic entity thresholds, hold time debouncing, and hysteresis to eliminate jitter.

data.name: Name
data.thresholds: Threshold Values (comma-separated numbers or entity IDs)

data_description.source_entity: Select a numeric sensor (e.g. temperature, battery, power, humidity, CO2) or input_number helper.
data_description.preset: Select a quick preset (e.g. Battery, Comfort Temp, Inside/Outside Range) or choose 'Custom'.
data_description.mode: Operating behavior: 'Multi-Tier Zones', 'Inside Range' (in bounds), 'Outside Range' (the inverted behavior: alerts outside bounds), 'Above Limit', or 'Below Limit'.
data_description.thresholds: Comma-separated numbers or entity IDs (e.g. '18, 24' or 'input_number.min_temp, 22.0, sensor.max_temp') for dynamic limits.
data_description.labels: Names for active states or zones separated by commas (e.g. 'inside, outside' or 'low, normal, high, critical').
data_description.hysteresis: WHAT IS HYSTERESIS? Hysteresis prevents rapid on/off flapping when a value hovers right on a boundary. Example: A limit of 20°C with 0.5°C hysteresis turns ON at 20.5°C and only turns OFF once falling below 19.5°C, ensuring clean switching without fluttering.
data_description.hold_time: Minimum seconds the value must continuously stay in the new state before switching (0 = instant). Filters out short measurement spikes.
data_description.gradient_threshold: Triggers a gradient alert when the measurement rises or falls faster than X units per minute (e.g. sudden temperature or power surge).

error.empty_source: Please select a numeric target entity.
error.empty_thresholds: Please specify at least one threshold value.
error.requires_two_thresholds: Inside and Outside Range modes require at least two thresholds (lower and upper bound).
error.invalid_thresholds: Thresholds must be comma-separated numbers or valid entity IDs (e.g. 18, 24 or input_number.limit).
